org.heroText: Association for Welfare, Social Action and Research India works with children, women, youth, and communities across education, health, livelihoods, research, and protection — building a more equitable society since 2001.
org.about: The name AWSAR means "opportunity" in Hindi. Founded by social entrepreneurs and students from the University of Delhi, AWSAR was built on the belief that access to opportunity is the foundation of all social and economic transformation. For over 25 years, AWSAR has partnered with communities, governments, corporate foundations, and international organisations to deliver evidence-based, sustainable development programmes.
org.aboutHeading: We believe every individual deserves an opportunity
org.vision: To create an inclusive and equitable society founded on democratic values, sustainable livelihoods, and an improved quality of life for all.
org.mission: To foster opportunities for holistic development by strengthening capacities, generating knowledge, and delivering diversified professional services that empower communities and institutions working with marginalised populations.
org.pillarsQuote: Welfare, Social Action and Research — three pillars that together create lasting change.

founderQuote.text: Access to opportunity is the game changer for children struggling in life. That is why we named this organisation AWSAR.

values.title: Dignity & Inclusion
values.text: Every person we serve — regardless of caste, gender, religion, or background — deserves to be treated with full dignity. We design for inclusion and refuse to work in ways that marginalise further.

values.title: Evidence Over Assumption
values.text: We measure what we do, share what we find, and change course when the evidence says we should. Good intentions have to be matched by honest results.

values.title: Community Ownership
values.text: We build capacity, not dependency. Our aim is always to make ourselves unnecessary, leaving behind people and systems that can sustain progress independently.

values.title: Transparency
values.text: Our finances, decisions and outcomes are open to scrutiny. Trust is built through consistency, not promises.

values.title: Compassion in Practice
values.text: We work with some of the most vulnerable people in India. Compassion is not a sentiment here — it shapes how we listen, how we design programmes, and how we measure success. Numbers matter; so do names.

values.title: Collaboration Over Competition
values.text: Development challenges are too large for any single organisation. We actively partner with government, CSR, academia, and civil society — believing that shared goals and combined strengths multiply impact for the communities we serve.

timeline.title: AWSAR is founded
timeline.text: Social entrepreneurs and University of Delhi students establish AWSAR. First community education work begins in East Delhi.

timeline.title: Registration & government recognition
timeline.text: Registered under the Societies Registration Act, Delhi. Receives support under CAPART's Starter Package to Young Professionals Scheme, Ministry of Rural Development.

timeline.title: Programmes deepen across sectors
timeline.text: AWSAR expands into child protection, CHILDLINE 1098 services (run by AWSAR until 2024), women's empowerment, health, and community development. Partnerships grow with DLF Foundation, Naandi Foundation, ERM India, and government ministries.

timeline.title: Research and evidence leadership
timeline.text: Major field assignments — Manesar Survey, HUNGaMA nutrition study, CHILDLINE situational analysis across NCR cities, and the Jhajjar Social Impact Assessment — establish AWSAR's research credentials.

timeline.title: COVID response and renewal
timeline.text: AWSAR delivers food distribution, health support, and COVID-19 awareness in slums and rural communities. Model Village initiative launches in Dankaur, Gautam Budh Nagar, UP.

programmes.summary: Socio-economic surveys, needs assessments, baseline studies, social impact assessments, M&E, and data analysis for development decisions.
programmes.intro: AWSAR conducts rigorous field research to help governments, donors, corporates, and development organisations make informed decisions.

portfolio.title: Manesar Socio-Economic Household Survey
portfolio.text: Comprehensive baseline across 10 villages covering livelihoods, education, health, and social conditions. Commissioned by DLF Foundation.

portfolio.title: HUNGaMA Nutrition Survey
portfolio.text: Field contribution to Naandi Foundation's national study on hunger and malnutrition across Uttar Pradesh — 1.6M+ national context.

portfolio.title: CHILDLINE Situational Analysis — NCR
portfolio.text: Three-city analysis of child protection service environments covering 3,000 respondents across children, police, and community stakeholders.

portfolio.title: Jhajjar Social Impact Assessment
portfolio.text: Census survey of four villages for ERM India, assessing socioeconomic conditions and social impact of planned industrial development.

programmes.summary: Protecting children from abuse, neglect, trafficking, and child labour through rescue, rehabilitation, and community systems.
programmes.intro: Every child deserves a safe, nurturing, protective environment. AWSAR works to protect children from abuse, neglect, exploitation, trafficking, child labour, and child marriage.
interventions: Rescue and rehabilitation of children in distress
Child rights awareness in communities and schools
Prevention of child labour and trafficking
Child safety programmes and school safety

programmes.summary: Early childhood education centres, brick-kiln education, school infrastructure improvement, and foundational literacy and numeracy support.
programmes.intro: AWSAR brings education to children who would otherwise be left behind — at brick kilns, in slums, and in communities with limited school access.

programmes.summary: Preventive healthcare, maternal and child health, mental health and psychosocial support, and telemedicine for rural communities.
programmes.intro: AWSAR delivers community health initiatives that address the gap in preventive healthcare access for marginalised populations.

programmes.summary: Vocational training, livelihood skills, sanitary pad production, financial inclusion, self-help groups, and women's leadership programmes.
programmes.intro: Economic independence is central to women's empowerment. AWSAR equips women with marketable skills, financial literacy, and leadership capabilities.

impact.label: Women & girls trained in livelihood skills

programmes.summary: Emergency food, shelter, relief kits, COVID-19 ration distribution, and community health and awareness in crisis situations.
programmes.intro: When crisis strikes, AWSAR mobilises rapidly to provide emergency relief and community support to the most vulnerable.

programmes.summary: National Environment Awareness Campaigns, climate-resilient agriculture, tree plantation, water conservation, and rainwater harvesting.
programmes.intro: AWSAR integrates environmental sustainability into its community development work, building climate resilience at the grassroots.

programmes.summary: Integrated rural development — education, healthcare, agriculture, digital inclusion, and environmental sustainability.
programmes.intro: AWSAR's Model Village initiative in Dankaur, Gautam Budh Nagar, UP, is a holistic approach to rural development.

impact.label: Model Village launched, Gautam Budh Nagar, UP

programmes.summary: Organisational development, capacity building, programme design, training modules, and advisory services for NGOs and government bodies.
programmes.intro: AWSAR provides technical support and institutional capacity building to NGOs, government bodies, and corporate foundations.

volunteer.title: Give your time. Change a life.
volunteer.intro: Volunteering with AWSAR means showing up — for children at brick-kiln education centres, for women in livelihood programmes, for communities rebuilding after crisis. No prior NGO experience required; just willingness and reliability. We match your skills and availability to the right programme.
volunteer.commitment: At least 4 hours per week for a minimum of 8 weeks. This ensures continuity for the communities you work with, and a meaningful experience for you.

areas.title: Teaching & Tutoring
areas.text: Support children at brick-kiln education centres and remedial reading programmes across Delhi NCR. Any teaching background welcome.

areas.title: Digital & Vocational Skills
areas.text: Teach computer literacy, professional skills, and digital tools to youth and women's self-help groups.

areas.title: Health & Awareness Camps
areas.text: Assist preventive healthcare outreach, maternal health workshops, and mental health awareness sessions. Medical background a plus, not required.

areas.title: Research & Data Support
areas.text: Help with field surveys, data entry, and report writing. Ideal for social science, statistics, or development studies students.

areas.title: Communications & Creative
areas.text: Design IEC materials, photograph field activities, write field stories, or manage AWSAR's social media presence.

areas.title: Disaster Relief Support
areas.text: Help coordinate relief distributions, ration kits, and community awareness during emergency response operations.
